_about: What a Craft or Profession rank does away from the benches (rules/tradecraft.py). The owner
chose options A, B and C of docs/craft-profession-options.md on 2026-10-07 (not D, named
trades; not E, background skills). Each row is a rule the engine cites: the GM names WHICH
use and the rule supplies the skill, the DC, the time, the cost and the pay. No model writes
This game keeps one Craft and one Profession: Craft (weapons), Craft (armor) and the rest
are all the one Craft, and a trade name folds onto its base (rules/tables.py base_skill).
Every field marked HOUSE departs from the book, and its source says what it departs from.

judge-make.name: judging a thing's make
judge-make.source: Pathfinder Unchained p.51, Expanded Craft (aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=1742): 'Identify masterwork armor on sight' (Craft (armor)) DC 15, 'Identify a masterwork weapon on sight' (Craft (weapons)) DC 15, 'Identify a masterwork bow on sight' (Craft (bows)) DC 15; 'Determine an item's hardness and hit points' DC 20, trained only.
judge-make.house: HOUSE: one Craft answers for every trade's row (option D was not chosen). The DC 20 row is read as the same look beaten by 5 rather than a second roll.
judge-make.once_a_day: The same thing judged again the same day tells nothing new (CRB Appraise: 'Additional attempts to Appraise an item reveal the same result').

mend-gear.name: mending ordinary gear
mend-gear.source: CRB p.91, Craft: 'You can repair an item by making checks against the same DC that it took to make the item in the first place. The cost of repairing an item is one-fifth of the item's price.' Try Again: 'each time you fail by 5 or more, you ruin half the raw materials.' CRB Conditions, Broken: repairing 'requires a DC 20 Craft check and 1 hour of work per point of damage'; magic items 'can only be repaired with a mending or make whole spell'. CRB Smashing an Object: a ruined (0 hit point) object is not repaired by Craft.
mend-gear.house: HOUSE, choosing between the CRB's two answers: the Craft entry's DC (the making DC, from the table below) and cost (one-fifth), and the Broken condition's time (1 hour a point), because the Craft entry states no time. The DC 20 is the floor for masterwork work (the masterwork component's own Craft DC) and the DC for a thing the table cannot place.
mend-gear.dc_source: CRB p.91, Craft DCs table: armor or shield 10 + AC bonus; longbow, shortbow or arrows 12; composite bows 15; simple melee or thrown weapon 12; martial 15; exotic 18; crossbow or bolts 15; typical item (iron pot) 10; complex or superior item 20.

trade-question.name: a question of the trade
trade-question.source: CRB, Profession: 'You can answer questions about your Profession. Basic questions are DC 10, while more complex questions are DC 15 or higher.'
trade-question.house: HOUSE: the CRB names no number above 15, so 'or higher' is not offered — an obscure question is complex. On a success the tell names the places here where that trade works (the engine's own place list, never a name the model makes up).

haggle.name: haggling at a counter
haggle.source: Ultimate Campaign p.138, Bargaining (aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=1341): the buyer's Bluff against the seller's Sense Motive sets an Undercut Percentage, '2%, plus 1% for every point by which the Bluff check exceeds the Sense Motive check (minimum 0%)', and 'the lowest amount the seller will accept is 75% of this Asking Price'.
haggle.house: HOUSE (the owner's option B, 2026-10-07): Profession stands where the book has Bluff — Ultimate Campaign never names Profession (merchant) — and the keeper answers with Sense Motive. The undercut stops at 25%, the book's 75% floor. It is mirrored for a sale (the shop pays that much more), which the book's bargaining (a buyer's procedure) does not cover. Once a counter a day; a failed haggle leaves the list price.

day-work.name: a day's paid work
day-work.source: Pathfinder Second Edition, Player Core p.228, Earn Income, and its Table 4-2: Income Earned (2e.aonprd.com/Actions.aspx?ID=2364): pay by task level and proficiency, not by the d20's total; a critical success pays as a task one level higher, a failure pays the Failed column, a critical failure pays nothing. GM Core p.52-53: the DC is the task level's (Table 10-5), and 'the highest-level task available is usually the same as the level of the settlement' — village 0-1, town 2-4, city 5-7. CRB, Profession: 'An untrained laborer can earn an average of 1 silver piece per day.'
day-work.house: HOUSE: PF2e's table in PF1's coin. PF2e prices on a silver standard; its amounts are multiplied by coin_scale. First set at 10, anchored on two published pairs: an untrained day (PF1 CRB 1 sp; PF2e's failed task 0, 1 cp) and a dagger (PF1 2 gp; PF2e 2 sp). The owner halved it to 5 on 2026-10-07 ('Paid work: halve it'): at 10 a level-3 character in a city earned 5 gp a day on a success, 35 gp a week, about four times the CRB's half-the-check wage; at 5 it is 2 gp 5 sp a day, 17 gp 5 sp a week. The untrained wage below is the CRB's own 1 sp and is not scaled. Proficiency is read from ranks at the character levels PF2e first allows each (expert at 3, master at 7, legendary at 15). The task is the lower of the character's level and the settlement's highest task. PF2e's natural 20 and 1 are not applied: 1e excludes them from skill checks (CRB p.180). A day is 8 hours of work charged to the body, then the evening fed, watered and slept, as a day on the road is (Engine._march).

pay_cp_by_task._units: copper pieces per day, PF2e's own figures before coin_scale
